title: Why Every Luxury Soon Feels Normal (Hedonic Adaptation)
alt_title_1: The 90-Day Brain Glitch Behind Lifestyle Creep
alt_title_2: How to Escape the Hedonic Treadmill Without Deprivation
description_hook: In 1971, psychologists Philip Brickman and Donald Campbell described why big material upgrades fade into the background while the monthly bills last for years. Here is the Intentional Contrast protocol to beat hedonic adaptation.

scenes.headline: When Luxury Turns Into Wallpaper
scenes.stat_label: UNTIL MAJOR UPGRADES FEEL COMPLETELY ORDINARY
bullets: Day one brings a rush of novelty
Weeks later, it feels normal again
scenes.narration: Nearly every expensive upgrade you crave right now will start to feel like background wallpaper surprisingly fast.
scenes.source: Brickman & Campbell, 'Hedonic relativism and planning the good society' (1971)

scenes.headline: Brickman & Campbell's Hedonic Treadmill
bullets: Human nervous systems detect changes, not static comfort
Even major windfalls snap back toward baseline mood
scenes.narration: In 1971, psychologists Philip Brickman and Donald Campbell described the hedonic treadmill: people adapt to nicer apartments, newer cars, and bigger screens, and their happiness drifts back toward where it started.
scenes.source: Brickman & Campbell (1971); Brickman, Coates & Janoff-Bulman, lottery winners study (1978)

scenes.headline: 90 Days of Thrill for 60 Months of Bills
scenes.left_body: 60-month luxury lease -> novelty gone by Month 3
scenes.right_body: Lean monthly overhead + rare debt-free treats that stay vivid
scenes.narration: The financial trap is asymmetric. The dopamine rush of a luxury lease evaporates in three months, while the fixed monthly bill stays locked in for five years.

scenes.headline: The Intentional Contrast Protocol
scenes.stat_label: LEAN BASELINE + RARE TREATS = HIGH MARGIN
scenes.stat_subtext: Scarcity preserves joy while surplus cash compounds
scenes.narration: To escape without feeling deprived, practice Intentional Contrast: keep your monthly baseline lean, then enjoy occasional debt-free experiences that stay special because they are rare.

scenes.headline: Quarterly 7-Day Simplicity Reset
bullets: Pause non-essential spending for 1 week per quarter
Bank the margin and restore sensitivity to simple wins
scenes.narration: Run a seven-day simplicity reset every quarter so ordinary comforts feel rich again and your savings compound untouched, especially once you realize...
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
